name_reason: Name already conforms: data_fd2_ prefix (game global data), domain 'chapter', descriptor 'ch30_end_scene_char_pos_x_table'. 'ch30' is the chapter-30 domain ID (meaningful, must be preserved, not an address residue), 'end_scene' marks it as used by the chapter-30 end handler, 'char_pos_x' = per-character world tile X coordinate, 'table' reflects the array data type. No Ghidra address residue (no hex suffix equal to its address 0x52327). Verified accurate against contents and the sole reader.
purpose: Chapter-30 end-scene (GOOD ENDING) per-character world tile X-coordinate table; supplies the X positions where the surviving cast (char slots 0..0x13) are placed for the final scene.
logic_summary: First of three sibling 20-byte tables (pos_x @0x52327, pos_y @0x5233B, facing @0x5234F). Sole reader fd2_chapter_30_end @0x25757 copies all 20 bytes into a stack scratch buffer (5 dwords via MOVSD x5) and passes the buffer as arg1 (pos_x) to fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro(pos_x, pos_y, facing, 0, 0x13, ...), which indexes the bytes by char slot to set each character's pos_x. Boundaries confirmed: pos_y's reader xref at 0x25785 targets 0x5233B and facing's at 0x25793 targets 0x5234F, exactly 20 bytes apart, so this table is byte[20].
element_semantics: Element i = world-map tile X coordinate for runtime character slot i (i = 0..0x13). Values: 0x16,0x16,0x14,0x15,0x17,0x18,0x14,0x15,0x17,0x18,0x14,0x15,0x16,0x17,0x18,0x14,0x15,0x16,0x17,0x18 (a 5-column formation: rows place slots at X in 0x14..0x18 with the two leaders at 0x16).
notes: is_const=true derived from Ghidra game-side xrefs being READ/DATA only (0x25775, 0x25785, 0x25793 etc; no writers). src already declares 'const uint8 ...[20]' and the comment block @ chend2.c lines 928-936 already documents all three sibling tables accurately and concisely, so comment_verdict=keep (no Edit to chend2.c). Data plate at 0x52327 was blank (<null>); created a concise plate via run_script_inline PLATE_COMMENT per project_ghidra_data_plate_mechanism (set_plate_comment fails on data addresses). No rename applied this stage (verdict keep anyway).
